subproblems.title: Lusin's theorem, compact form, for measurable maps into a second-countable space (finite-measure set)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let Y be a second-countable topological space (Y : Type) carrying a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. Let μ be any measure on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P = Euclid P, let A ⊆ ℝ^P be measurable with μ(A) < ∞, let g : ℝ^P → Y be measurable, and let ε ∈ [0, ∞] with ε ≠ 0. Then there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε such that g is continuous on K (ContinuousOn g K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Y) (ε : ℝ≥0∞), Measurable g → MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → ε ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < ε ∧ ContinuousOn g K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Status. This is the accepted declaration Submission.dor_ims_lusin_measurable_continuousOn (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.imrep_mass_and_support-a1.lusin_covector-a1.lusin_measurable-a1, candidate commit e4172a7b), reused here with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is its reviewed proof.
Source. Step 3 of the parent proof applies Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 1.17; chapter-01.txt lines 344–380) on sets of finite measure. Here it is proved in the compact form for an arbitrary second-countable target Y, which makes the parent's coordinatewise treatment of Du unnecessary. The argument is the standard countable-basis proof. The budget ε·2^{−k−2} is replaced by summable weights, which also covers ε = ∞.
1. (Inner regularity inside A.) Let ν be μ restricted to A, so ν(E) = μ(E ∩ A) for measurable E.
- ν is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, since ν(ℝ^P) = μ(A) < ∞; in particular it is locally finite.
- ℝ^P is a σ-compact (indeed proper) metric space, so ν is regular (Mathlib instance Regular.of_sigmaCompactSpace_of_isLocallyFiniteMeasure). Hence ν is inner regular by compact sets on measurable sets of finite measure (MeasurableSet.exists_isCompact_sdiff_lt).
- Consequently, for every measurable E ⊆ A and every η ∈ (0, ∞] there is a compact F ⊆ E with ν(E ∖ F) < η.
- F is compact in a Hausdorff space, hence closed and measurable. So E ∖ F is a measurable subset of A, and ν(E ∖ F) = μ((E ∖ F) ∩ A) = μ(E ∖ F). Thus μ(E ∖ F) < η.
2. (Countable basis.) Fix a countable basis 𝓑 of the topology of Y. Y is nonempty (it contains g(0)) and ⋃𝓑 = Y, so 𝓑 ≠ ∅. Enumerate 𝓑 = {O_k : k ∈ ℕ}, with repetitions allowed. Each O_k is open, hence measurable in Y, so S_k := g⁻¹(O_k) is a measurable subset of ℝ^P because g is measurable.
3. (Weights.) Put δ := min(ε, 1) ∈ (0, 1] and η_k := δ·2^{−k−2} ∈ (0, ∞) for k ∈ ℕ. Then Σ_k η_k = δ/2 < δ ≤ ε; the middle inequality is strict because 0 < δ < ∞.
4. (Compact pieces.) Fix k. A ∩ S_k and A ∖ S_k are measurable subsets of A.
- By step 1 with η = η_k/2, choose compact sets C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k with μ((A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k) < η_k/2 and μ((A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k) < η_k/2.
- Put E_k := C_k ∪ D_k, a compact subset of A.
- If x ∈ A ∖ E_k, then x ∈ (A ∩ S_k) ∖ C_k when g(x) ∈ O_k, and x ∈ (A ∖ S_k) ∖ D_k otherwise. So subadditivity gives μ(A ∖ E_k) < η_k/2 + η_k/2 = η_k.
5. (The compact set.) Let K := ⋂_k E_k.
- Each E_k is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed, so K is closed.
- K lies in the compact set E_0, so K is compact, and K ⊆ E_0 ⊆ A.
- Since A ∖ K = ⋃_k (A ∖ E_k), countable subadditivity and steps 3–4 give μ(A ∖ K) ≤ Σ_k μ(A ∖ E_k) ≤ Σ_k η_k < ε.
6. (Continuity.) Fix k and x ∈ K, so x ∈ E_k = C_k ∪ D_k.
- If x ∉ D_k, then x ∈ C_k ⊆ S_k, so g(x) ∈ O_k.
- If g(x) ∈ O_k, then x ∈ S_k, so x ∉ D_k because D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k.
Hence K ∩ g⁻¹(O_k) = K ∩ (ℝ^P ∖ D_k). D_k is compact, hence closed, so this set is open in the subspace topology of K. Every open subset of Y is a union of sets O_k, so its preimage under the restriction g|_K : K → Y is a union of open subsets of K, hence open. Therefore g|_K is continuous (IsTopologicalBasis.continuous_iff), i.e. ContinuousOn g K.
By steps 5 and 6, K is a compact subset of A with μ(A ∖ K) < ε on which g is continuous. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν = μ restricted to A is a finite Borel measure on the σ-compact metric space ℝ^P, hence regular. Every measurable E ⊆ A therefore contains a compact F with μ(E ∖ F) arbitrarily small.
Enumerate a countable basis (O_k) of Y; each S_k = g⁻¹(O_k) is measurable.
Weights η_k = min(ε,1)·2^{−k−2} satisfy Σ η_k < ε.
Choose compact C_k ⊆ A ∩ S_k and D_k ⊆ A ∖ S_k with defects < η_k/2; then E_k = C_k ∪ D_k satisfies μ(A ∖ E_k) < η_k.
K = ⋂ E_k is compact, K ⊆ A and μ(A ∖ K) < ε.
On K, g(x) ∈ O_k ⇔ x ∉ D_k, so preimages of basic open sets are relatively open and g is continuous on K.

subproblems.title: Lusin's theorem on all of ℝ^n with a closed set (sets of infinite measure)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let Y be a second-countable topological space (Y : Type) carrying a σ-algebra in which every open set is measurable. Let g : ℝ^n → Y be measurable and let B ⊆ ℝ^n = Euclid n be measurable, possibly of infinite Lebesgue measure. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that g is continuous on C and L^n(B ∖ C) < ε, where L^n = volume.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] [MeasurableSpace Y] [OpensMeasurableSpace Y] (g : Euclid n → Y) (B : Set (Euclid n)), Measurable g → MeasurableSet B → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ C : Set (Euclid n), C ⊆ B ∧ IsClosed C ∧ ContinuousOn g C ∧ volume (B \ C) < ε
subproblems.natural_proof:
Status. This is the accepted declaration Submission.codim1_rdo_c1a_lusin_isClosed (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.rectifiable_density_one-a1.c1_approximation-a1.lusin_closed-a1, candidate commit 1ebfef61, whose history contains the sibling lusin_finite), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is its reviewed proof.
Source. This is step 3 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon's sentence in the proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 246–251): 'By Lusin's theorem (which applies to sets of infinite measure for L^n) there is a closed set C ⊆ B such that ∇f|C is continuous'.
- As in the parent proof, the passage from finite to infinite measure is made on bounded shells. This is Simon's own device for the infinite-measure case of Ch. 1, 1.15(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 333–342).
- On each shell the sibling lusin_finite is applied. It allows any second-countable target, so the parent's coordinatewise treatment and its budget ε·2^{−j−3}/m are replaced by the budget below.
Notation: L^n = volume on ℝ^n; |·| is the Euclidean norm; B(x, ρ) is the open ball and B̄(x, ρ) the closed ball.
1. (Shells.) For j ∈ ℕ let S_j := {x ∈ ℝ^n : j ≤ |x| < j + 1}.
- Each S_j is Borel, being the intersection of a closed and an open preimage under the continuous norm.
- S_j ⊆ B̄(0, j + 1), so L^n(S_j) < ∞.
- Every x lies in S_{⌊|x|⌋}.
2. (Local finiteness.) Let F_j ⊆ S_j for j ∈ ℕ. Then the family (F_j)_j is locally finite: for x ∈ ℝ^n, if y ∈ B(x, 1) ∩ F_j then j ≤ |y| < |x| + 1. So B(x, 1) meets F_j only for the finitely many j < |x| + 1.
3. (Budget.) Put δ := min(ε, 1) ∈ (0, 1] and δ_j := δ/2^{j+2} > 0 for j ∈ ℕ. Then Σ_j δ_j = δ/2 < δ ≤ ε; the middle inequality is strict because 0 < δ < ∞.
4. (Lusin on each shell.) Fix j. The set B_j := B ∩ S_j is measurable with L^n(B_j) ≤ L^n(S_j) < ∞, and δ_j ≠ 0.
- Apply the sibling lusin_finite with P = n, the space Y, μ = L^n, A = B_j, the map g and ε = δ_j.
- It gives a compact K_j ⊆ B_j with L^n(B_j ∖ K_j) < δ_j such that g is continuous on K_j.
- K_j is closed, being compact in a Hausdorff space.
5. (Gluing.) Put C := ⋃_j K_j. Then C ⊆ ⋃_j B_j ⊆ B. Since K_j ⊆ S_j, the family (K_j) is locally finite by step 2.
- A locally finite union of closed sets is closed (LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion), so C is closed.
- A map continuous on each member of a locally finite family of closed sets is continuous on their union (LocallyFinite.continuousOn_iUnion). Concretely, near x ∈ C only finitely many K_j occur, and the pasting lemma for finitely many closed sets applies.
- Hence g is continuous on C.
6. (Measure.) Let x ∈ B ∖ C and j := ⌊|x|⌋. Then x ∈ B ∩ S_j = B_j, and x ∉ K_j because K_j ⊆ C. Hence B ∖ C ⊆ ⋃_j (B_j ∖ K_j). Countable subadditivity and steps 3–4 give L^n(B ∖ C) ≤ Σ_j L^n(B_j ∖ K_j) ≤ Σ_j δ_j = δ/2 < δ ≤ ε.
Thus C is a closed subset of B on which g is continuous, with L^n(B ∖ C) < ε. ∎
proof_key_steps: Bounded Borel shells S_j = {j ≤ |x| < j+1} cover ℝ^n, and any family F_j ⊆ S_j is locally finite.
Budget δ = min(ε,1), δ_j = δ/2^{j+2}, so Σ δ_j = δ/2 < ε.
lusin_finite on the finite-measure set B ∩ S_j gives a compact K_j ⊆ B ∩ S_j with L^n((B ∩ S_j) ∖ K_j) < δ_j and g continuous on K_j.
C = ⋃ K_j is closed and g is continuous on C, by local finiteness. B ∖ C ⊆ ⋃ ((B ∩ S_j) ∖ K_j) has measure ≤ δ/2 < ε.

subproblems.title: Egoroff's theorem on ℝ^n with a closed good set and uniform convergence on its compact subsets
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let C ⊆ ℝ^n = Euclid n be measurable, let η_k : ℝ^n → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) and g : ℝ^n → ℝ be Borel measurable, and suppose that η_k(x) → g(x) as k → ∞ for every x ∈ C. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed set A ⊆ C with L^n(C ∖ A) < ε (L^n = volume) such that η_k → g uniformly on every compact set Q ⊆ A.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : Set (Euclid n)) (η : ℕ → Euclid n → ℝ) (g : Euclid n → ℝ), MeasurableSet C → (∀ k, Measurable (η k)) → Measurable g → (∀ x ∈ C, Tendsto (fun k => η k x) atTop (𝓝 (g x))) → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ A : Set (Euclid n), A ⊆ C ∧ IsClosed A ∧ volume (C \ A) < ε ∧ ∀ Q : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → TendstoUniformlyOn η g atTop Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Status. This is the accepted declaration Submission.codim1_rdo_c1a_egorov_isClosed (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.rectifiable_density_one-a1.c1_approximation-a1.egorov_closed-a1, candidate commit e90d4d35), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is its reviewed proof.
Source. This is step 5 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon's sentences in the proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 260–265): 'by Egoroff's Theorem (applied to the finite measure sets C ∩ B_j(0), j = 1, 2, …) there is an L^n-measurable set A₀ ⊆ C such that L^n(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4 and η_k converges uniformly to zero on each bounded subset of A₀. Since we can take a closed set A ⊆ A₀ with L^n(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/4 …'.
- Here the limit is a general measurable g.
- As in the parent proof, the closed subset is produced on bounded shells (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15(2), chapter-01.txt lines 333–342), because A₀ may have infinite measure.
- The budgets δ/2^{j+3} with δ = min(ε, 1) replace the parent's ε·2^{−j−5}.
Notation: L^n = volume on ℝ^n; B_ρ(0) is the open ball; S_j := {x : j ≤ |x| < j + 1}.
1. (Budget.) Put δ := min(ε, 1) ∈ (0, 1] and δ_j := δ/2^{j+3} > 0 for j ∈ ℕ, so Σ_j δ_j = δ/4.
2. (Egoroff on bounded pieces.) Fix j ∈ ℕ. C_j := C ∩ B_{j+1}(0) is measurable with L^n(C_j) ≤ L^n(B_{j+1}(0)) < ∞.
- The η_k and g are real-valued and measurable, hence strongly measurable, and η_k(x) → g(x) for every x ∈ C_j.
- Apply Egoroff's theorem (Mathlib tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto) with the real tolerance δ_j. Its almost-everywhere hypothesis holds everywhere here.
- It gives a measurable t_j ⊆ C_j with L^n(t_j) ≤ δ_j such that η_k → g uniformly on C_j ∖ t_j.
3. (The set A₀.) Put A₀ := C ∖ ⋃_j t_j, a measurable subset of C.
- C ∖ A₀ ⊆ ⋃_j t_j, so L^n(C ∖ A₀) ≤ Σ_j L^n(t_j) ≤ δ/4.
- Let Q ⊆ A₀ be bounded. Then Q ⊆ B_R(0) for some R > 0, hence Q ⊆ B_{j+1}(0) for any j ∈ ℕ with j ≥ R.
- Also Q ⊆ A₀ ⊆ C and Q ∩ t_j = ∅, so Q ⊆ C_j ∖ t_j.
- By step 2 and restriction of uniform convergence to a subset, η_k → g uniformly on Q.
4. (Shells.) Each S_j is Borel and bounded, hence of finite measure. The S_j are pairwise disjoint and cover ℝ^n, since x ∈ S_{⌊|x|⌋}. Any family F_j ⊆ S_j is locally finite: B(x, 1) meets F_j only if j ≤ |y| < |x| + 1 for some y, i.e. only for finitely many j.
5. (Closed inner regularity.) Fix j. A₀ ∩ S_j is measurable of finite measure. Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n is regular, hence weakly regular, so it is inner regular by closed sets on measurable sets of finite measure (MeasurableSet.exists_isClosed_sdiff_lt). Choose a closed F_j ⊆ A₀ ∩ S_j with L^n((A₀ ∩ S_j) ∖ F_j) < δ_j.
6. (The closed set.) Put A := ⋃_j F_j.
- By step 4 the family (F_j) is locally finite, so A is closed (LocallyFinite.isClosed_iUnion). Also A ⊆ A₀ ⊆ C.
- If x ∈ A₀ ∖ A and j := ⌊|x|⌋, then x ∈ (A₀ ∩ S_j) ∖ F_j. Hence A₀ ∖ A ⊆ ⋃_j ((A₀ ∩ S_j) ∖ F_j), and L^n(A₀ ∖ A) ≤ Σ_j δ_j = δ/4.
- Since C ∖ A ⊆ (C ∖ A₀) ∪ (A₀ ∖ A), L^n(C ∖ A) ≤ δ/4 + δ/4 = δ/2 < δ ≤ ε. The middle inequality is strict because 0 < δ < ∞.
7. (Uniform convergence on compact subsets.) Let Q ⊆ A be compact. Then Q is bounded and Q ⊆ A ⊆ A₀, so η_k → g uniformly on Q by step 3. ∎
proof_key_steps: Budget δ = min(ε,1), δ_j = δ/2^{j+3}.
Egoroff on the finite-measure sets C ∩ B_{j+1}(0) gives t_j with L^n(t_j) ≤ δ_j. A₀ = C ∖ ⋃ t_j loses at most δ/4, and η_k → g uniformly on every bounded subset of A₀.
Closed inner regularity on the shells A₀ ∩ S_j gives closed sets F_j. A = ⋃ F_j is closed by local finiteness, and L^n(C ∖ A) ≤ δ/2 < ε.
A compact Q ⊆ A is a bounded subset of A₀, so the convergence is uniform on Q.

subproblems.title: Whitney's compatibility condition 1.6(∗) for a Lipschitz function on a large closed subset (the η_k argument of Simon 1.5)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and L ≥ 0, let f : ℝ^n → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (ℝ^n = Euclid n), and let C ⊆ ℝ^n be closed such that f is differentiable at every x ∈ C and x ↦ Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x is continuous on C. Then for every ε ∈ (0, ∞] there is a closed set A ⊆ C with L^n(C ∖ A) < ε (L^n = volume) such that for every compact Q ⊆ A and every ε' > 0 there is δ > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε'|y − x| for all x ∈ Q and all y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : Euclid n → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (C : Set (Euclid n)), LipschitzWith L f → IsClosed C → (∀ x ∈ C, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → ContinuousOn (fderiv ℝ f) C → ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∃ A : Set (Euclid n), A ⊆ C ∧ IsClosed A ∧ volume (C \ A) < ε ∧ ∀ Q : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → ∀ ε' : ℝ, 0 < ε' → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ Q, ∀ y ∈ A, dist x y < δ → ‖f y - f x - fderiv ℝ f x (y - x)‖ ≤ ε' * ‖y - x‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Status. This is the accepted declaration Submission.codim1_rdo_c1a_whitney_remainder (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.rectifiable_density_one-a1.c1_approximation-a1.whitney_remainder-a1, candidate commit 756999fd, whose history contains the sibling egorov_closed), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is its reviewed proof.
Source. These are steps 4 and 6 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon's proof of Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5 (chapter-02.txt lines 251–265).
- On C one defines R(x, y). Simon notes that lim_{y→x, y∈C} R(x, y) = 0 for x ∈ C, 'but not necessarily uniformly'.
- He puts η_k(x) = sup{|R(x, y)| : y ∈ C ∩ B_{1/k}(x) ∖ {x}}, so η_k ↓ 0 pointwise on C. Egoroff gives uniform convergence on a large closed A, 'and 1.6(∗) holds'.
- Here η is indexed from 0 with radius 1/(k + 1) (the parent's η_{k+1}), and R is taken in absolute value.
- Step 5 of the parent proof (Egoroff and the closed subset) is the sibling egorov_closed.
Notation: Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x ∈ (ℝ^n)*; |·| is the Euclidean norm and ‖·‖ the operator norm; L^n = volume.
1. (The remainder and its bound.) For x ≠ y let R(x, y) := |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| / |y − x| ≥ 0. Since f is L-Lipschitz, ‖Df(x)‖ ≤ L for every x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Hence R(x, y) ≤ (|f(y) − f(x)| + ‖Df(x)‖·|y − x|)/|y − x| ≤ 2L.
2. (Pointwise smallness.) Let x ∈ C. Since f is differentiable at x with derivative Df(x), for every ε'' > 0 there is ρ > 0 such that |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε''|y − x| whenever |y − x| < ρ.
3. (The functions η_k.) For k ∈ ℕ and x ∈ ℝ^n let E_k(x) := {R(x, y) : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k + 1)} ⊆ [0, 2L].
- Put η_k(x) := sup E_k(x) if x ∈ C (with sup ∅ := 0), and η_k(x) := 0 if x ∉ C. Then 0 ≤ η_k ≤ 2L.
- Since E_k(x) is bounded above, R(x, y) ≤ η_k(x) for all x, y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k + 1).
4. (Pointwise convergence.) Let x ∈ C and ε'' > 0. Take ρ from step 2 for ε''/2, and k₀ with 1/(k₀ + 1) < ρ.
- Let k ≥ k₀. Every y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k + 1) ≤ 1/(k₀ + 1) < ρ satisfies R(x, y) ≤ ε''/2.
- So every element of E_k(x) is ≤ ε''/2, and 0 ≤ η_k(x) ≤ ε''/2 < ε''.
Hence η_k(x) → 0 as k → ∞, for every x ∈ C.
5. (Borel measurability.) Fix k. By measurable_of_Ioi it suffices to show that {η_k > t} is Borel for every real t.
- If t < 0, the set is ℝ^n, because η_k ≥ 0.
- Let t ≥ 0 and U := {η_k > t}. Then U ⊆ C, since η_k = 0 ≤ t off C.
Claim: every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood W with W ∩ C ⊆ U.
- Let x ∈ U. Then x ∈ C, and E_k(x) ≠ ∅, since otherwise η_k(x) = sup ∅ = 0 ≤ t.
- As sup E_k(x) > t, some element of E_k(x) exceeds t: there is y ∈ C with 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k + 1) and R(x, y) > t.
- The map z ↦ R(z, y) is continuous within C at x. Its numerator z ↦ |f(y) − f(z) − Df(z)(y − z)| is continuous within C at x, because f is continuous (being Lipschitz), Df is continuous on C, and evaluation (λ, v) ↦ λ(v) is jointly continuous. Its denominator z ↦ |y − z| is continuous and non-zero at x.
- So the three conditions 0 < |y − z|, |y − z| < 1/(k + 1) and R(z, y) > t hold for all z ∈ C in some neighbourhood W of x.
- For z ∈ W ∩ C, step 3 (with z in place of x) gives η_k(z) ≥ R(z, y) > t, i.e. z ∈ U. This proves the claim.
Consequently U = C ∩ V, where V := interior(U ∪ (ℝ^n ∖ C)) is open:
- for x ∈ U, the claim gives W ⊆ U ∪ (ℝ^n ∖ C), so x ∈ V;
- conversely, C ∩ V ⊆ C ∩ (U ∪ (ℝ^n ∖ C)) ⊆ U.
C is closed and V is open, so U is Borel. Thus η_k is Borel measurable. (Equivalently, η_k is lower semicontinuous on C.)
6. (Egoroff.) C is closed, hence measurable. Apply the sibling egorov_closed with:
- the set C;
- the measurable functions η_k (k ∈ ℕ) of step 5;
- the measurable limit g ≡ 0, the convergence hypothesis being step 4;
- the given ε.
It gives a closed A ⊆ C with L^n(C ∖ A) < ε such that η_k → 0 uniformly on every compact Q ⊆ A.
7. (The uniform remainder estimate.) Let Q ⊆ A be compact and ε' > 0. By step 6 there is k with |η_k(x)| < ε' for all x ∈ Q. Put δ := 1/(k + 1) > 0, and let x ∈ Q and y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ.
- If y = x, the left side is |f(x) − f(x) − Df(x)(0)| = 0 ≤ ε'·0.
- Otherwise x, y ∈ A ⊆ C and 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k + 1), so step 3 gives R(x, y) ≤ η_k(x) < ε'. Multiplying by |y − x| > 0 gives |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| = R(x, y)·|y − x| ≤ ε'|y − x|.
Together with step 6, A is the required closed set. ∎
proof_key_steps: R(x,y) = |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)|/|y − x| ≤ 2L, because ‖Df‖ ≤ L.
η_k(x) = sup{R(x,y) : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/(k+1)} on C (0 off C) satisfies R(x,y) ≤ η_k(x), and η_k(x) → 0 on C by differentiability.
{η_k > t} is relatively open in the closed set C, by continuity of z ↦ R(z,y) within C (using continuity of f and of Df on C), so η_k is Borel.
egorov_closed gives a closed A ⊆ C with L^n(C ∖ A) < ε and η_k → 0 uniformly on each compact Q ⊆ A. Then |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ η_k(x)|y − x| ≤ ε'|y − x| for x ∈ Q, y ∈ A, |x − y| < 1/(k+1).

subproblems.title: Whitney's C¹ extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ ℝ^n = Euclid n be closed, and let h : ℝ^n → ℝ and D : ℝ^n → (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ) be continuous on A. Suppose that for every compact Q ⊆ A and every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that |h(y) − h(x) − D(x)(y − x)| ≤ ε|y − x| for all x ∈ Q and all y ∈ A with |x − y| < δ. Then there is a C¹ function g : ℝ^n → ℝ (ContDiff ℝ 1 g) with g = h on A and with Fréchet derivative D(a) at every a ∈ A (HasFDerivAt g (D a) a).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid n)) (h : Euclid n → ℝ) (D : Euclid n → (Euclid n →L[ℝ] ℝ)), IsClosed A → ContinuousOn h A → ContinuousOn D A → (∀ Q : Set (Euclid n), IsCompact Q → Q ⊆ A → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ x ∈ Q, ∀ y ∈ A, dist x y < δ → ‖h y - h x - D x (y - x)‖ ≤ ε * ‖y - x‖) → ∃ g : Euclid n → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 g ∧ EqOn g h A ∧ ∀ a ∈ A, HasFDerivAt g (D a) a
subproblems.natural_proof:
Status. This is the accepted declaration Submission.codim1_rdo_c1a_whitney_extension (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.rectifiable_density_one-a1.c1_approximation-a1.whitney_extension-a1, candidate commit 3c58a149), reused with its byte-identical frozen type. The proof below is its reviewed proof.
Source. This is step 7 of the parent proof.
- Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6 (chapter-02.txt lines 173–186) states the theorem but prints no proof. Line 186 says 'For the proof see for example [EG92] or [Fed69]', and Remark 1.7(2) treats only n = 1.
- The proof below is the standard Whitney-decomposition argument of [EG92] (Evans–Gariepy, Measure Theory and Fine Properties of Functions, §6.5).
- It is exactly the form kernel-checked in the pinned SimonGMT files Chapter02/WhitneyCover.lean, WhitneyPartition.lean, WhitneyJet.lean and WhitneyExtension.lean (theorem exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney). The three hypotheses above are the fields of SimonGMT's HasWhitneyC1Compatibility A h D.
Correction to the parent's import note. The parent proof suggests importing Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WhitneyExtension. That is not viable:
- WhitneyExtension has no .olean;
- the WhitneyCover, WhitneyJet and WhitneyPartition oleans are stale, dated 2026-10-03 against 2026-10-11 for the rest of SimonGMT;
- the comparator runs `lake build`, which would try to rebuild them on the read-only package tree.
The accepted declaration instead carries the construction inside Submission.lean, with no extra imports.
Notation: |·| is the Euclidean norm, ‖·‖ the operator norm on (ℝ^n)*, B(x, r) the open ball, B̄(x, r) the closed ball, and d(x) := dist(x, A).
0. (Trivial case and the radius function.) If A = ∅, take g := 0: it is C¹, and the other two conclusions are vacuous. Assume A ≠ ∅, and put r(x) := min(1, d(x))/100.
- Since d is 1-Lipschitz, |r(x) − r(y)| ≤ |x − y|/100.
- 0 ≤ r ≤ 1/100 and 100 r(x) ≤ d(x).
- Since A is closed, r(x) > 0 exactly when x ∉ A.
1. (Affine jets.) For b ∈ ℝ^n let P_b(x) := h(b) + D(b)(x − b). P_b is affine, hence C^∞, with derivative D(b) at every point, and P_b(b) = h(b). For all a, b, x,
 P_b(x) − P_a(x) = [h(b) − h(a) − D(a)(b − a)] + (D(b) − D(a))(x − b).
Hence |P_b(x) − P_a(x)| ≤ |h(b) − h(a) − D(a)(b − a)| + ‖D(b) − D(a)‖·|x − b|.
2. (Local uniform estimate.) Let a ∈ A and η > 0. Then there is δ ∈ (0, 1] such that
 (i) ‖D(b) − D(a)‖ ≤ η for all b ∈ A with |b − a| < δ, and
 (ii) |h(c) − h(b) − D(b)(c − b)| ≤ η|c − b| for all b, c ∈ A with |b − a| < δ and |c − a| < δ.
Proof:
- Q := A ∩ B̄(a, 1) is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^n), so the hypothesis gives r₀ > 0 for Q and η.
- Continuity of D on A at a gives η₀ > 0 with ‖D(b) − D(a)‖ < η for b ∈ A with |b − a| < η₀.
- Take δ := min(1, η₀, r₀/3). Then (i) holds by the choice of η₀.
- For (ii): b ∈ Q because |b − a| < δ ≤ 1, and |b − c| < 2δ < r₀. So the hypothesis applies with x = b and y = c.
3. (Nearest points.) A is closed and nonempty and ℝ^n is proper, so every x has a nearest point π(x) ∈ A with |x − π(x)| = d(x).
- For b ∈ A: |π(x) − b| ≤ |π(x) − x| + |x − b| ≤ 2|x − b|.
- For a ∈ A: π(a) = a.
4. (Whitney balls.) Apply the Vitali covering lemma (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_ball with τ = 4) to the balls B(x, r(x)), x ∈ ℝ^n ∖ A, whose radii are ≤ 1/100. It gives a set Z ⊆ ℝ^n ∖ A of centres such that:
- the balls B(c, r(c)), c ∈ Z, are pairwise disjoint;
- every x ∉ A satisfies |x − c| < 4r(c) for some c ∈ Z.
5. (Comparability and bounded overlap.) For x ∉ A let Z_x := {c ∈ Z : |x − c| ≤ r(x) + 10 r(c)}.
 (a) If c ∈ Z_x, then r(x)/2 ≤ r(c) ≤ 2r(x) and |x − c| ≤ 21 r(x). This follows from |r(x) − r(c)| ≤ |x − c|/100 ≤ (r(x) + 10 r(c))/100.
 (b) There is N ∈ ℕ, depending only on n, with #Z_x ≤ N for every x ∉ A:
 - The map c ↦ (c − x)/r(x) is injective and sends Z_x into B̄(0, 21).
 - Distinct c, c' ∈ Z satisfy |c − c'| ≥ r(c); otherwise c' ∈ B(c, r(c)) ∩ B(c', r(c')), contradicting disjointness.
 - With (a), the images of distinct elements of Z_x are therefore at distance ≥ r(c)/r(x) ≥ 1/2.
 - B̄(0, 21) is totally bounded, so fix a set of N points such that every point of B̄(0, 21) lies within distance < 1/4 of one of them. Assign to each image such a point. Two distinct images assigned the same point would be at distance < 1/2, so the assignment is injective and #Z_x ≤ N.
6. (Bumps.) Fix ψ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^n) with 0 ≤ ψ ≤ 1, ψ = 1 on B̄(0, 4) and ψ = 0 outside B(0, 8) (Mathlib ContDiffBump with radii 4 < 8). ψ is C¹ with compact support, hence Λ-Lipschitz for some Λ. For c ∈ Z put φ_c(x) := ψ((x − c)/r(c)). Then:
- φ_c is C^∞ and 0 ≤ φ_c ≤ 1;
- φ_c = 1 on B̄(c, 4r(c)) and φ_c = 0 outside B(c, 8r(c));
- φ_c is (Λ/r(c))-Lipschitz, so ‖Dφ_c(x)‖ ≤ Λ/r(c) for all x.
7. (Local finiteness.) Let x ∉ A and |y − x| < r(x).
- y ∉ A, since r(x) ≤ d(x)/100 < d(x).
- If c ∈ Z ∖ Z_x, then |y − c| ≥ |x − c| − |y − x| > 10 r(c) ≥ 8 r(c), so φ_c(y) = 0.
- Hence on B(x, r(x)) the function S := Σ_{c∈Z} φ_c equals the finite sum Σ_{c∈Z_x} φ_c. So S is C^∞ on the open set ℝ^n ∖ A.
- S(x) ≥ 1 for x ∉ A: by step 4 pick c ∈ Z with |x − c| < 4r(c); then c ∈ Z_x and φ_c(x) = 1.
8. (Partition of unity.) For x ∉ A and c ∈ Z put w_c(x) := φ_c(x)/S(x).
- Each w_c is C^∞ on ℝ^n ∖ A, and 0 ≤ w_c ≤ 1.
- By step 7, Σ_{c∈Z_x} w_c(y) = 1 for |y − x| < r(x). Hence Σ_{c∈Z_x} Dw_c(x) = 0.
- Dw_c = Dφ_c/S − φ_c·DS/S², with S ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ φ_c ≤ 1. So ‖Dw_c(x)‖ ≤ ‖Dφ_c(x)‖ + ‖DS(x)‖.
- For c ∈ Z_x, ‖Dφ_c(x)‖ ≤ Λ/r(c) ≤ 2Λ/r(x) by 5(a). Since DS(x) = Σ_{c∈Z_x} Dφ_c(x), we get ‖DS(x)‖ ≤ 2NΛ/r(x).
Therefore Σ_{c∈Z_x} ‖Dw_c(x)‖ ≤ M/r(x), where M := 2Λ(N + 1)² does not depend on x.
9. (The extension.) For c ∈ Z let b_c := π(c) ∈ A. Define g(x) := h(x) for x ∈ A and g(x) := Σ_{c∈Z} w_c(x) P_{b_c}(x) for x ∉ A. By step 7, near each x ∉ A this is the finite sum Σ_{c∈Z_x} w_c P_{b_c}. Hence g = h on A, g is C^∞ on ℝ^n ∖ A, and for x ∉ A
 Dg(x) = Σ_{c∈Z_x} [w_c(x) D(b_c) + P_{b_c}(x) Dw_c(x)].
10. (Anchor distances.) Let x ∉ A and c ∈ Z_x.
- d(c) ≤ d(x) + |x − c|, and |x − c| ≤ 21 r(x) ≤ (21/100) d(x).
- So |x − b_c| ≤ |x − c| + d(c) ≤ 2|x − c| + d(x) ≤ 2 d(x).
- Consequently, for a ∈ A, using d(x) ≤ |x − a|: |x − b_c| ≤ 2|x − a| and |b_c − a| ≤ |b_c − x| + |x − a| ≤ 3|x − a|.
11. (Dg = D on A.) Let a ∈ A and ε > 0. Take δ from step 2 with η := ε/5, and let |x − a| < δ/4. We show |g(x) − g(a) − D(a)(x − a)| ≤ ε|x − a|. Since g(a) = h(a), the left side is |g(x) − P_a(x)|.
- If x ∈ A: by 2(ii) with b = a and c = x, |h(x) − h(a) − D(a)(x − a)| ≤ (ε/5)|x − a|.
- If x ∉ A: since Σ_{c∈Z_x} w_c(x) = 1, g(x) − P_a(x) = Σ_{c∈Z_x} w_c(x)(P_{b_c}(x) − P_a(x)).
 - For c ∈ Z_x, step 10 gives |b_c − a| ≤ 3|x − a| < δ and |x − b_c| ≤ 2|x − a|.
 - Step 1 with step 2 ((ii) for b = a, c = b_c; (i) for b = b_c) gives |P_{b_c}(x) − P_a(x)| ≤ (ε/5)|b_c − a| + (ε/5)|x − b_c| ≤ (ε/5)(3 + 2)|x − a| = ε|x − a|.
 - A convex combination of numbers of absolute value ≤ ε|x − a| has absolute value ≤ ε|x − a|.
Hence g has Fréchet derivative D(a) at a (HasFDerivAt g (D a) a). With step 9, g is differentiable everywhere, Dg = D on A, and Dg is continuous at every point of the open set ℝ^n ∖ A.
12. (Dg is continuous at points of A.) Let a ∈ A and ε > 0. Put η := ε/(2(1 + 700M)), take δ ∈ (0, 1] from step 2 for this η, and let |x − a| < δ/4.
- If x ∈ A: by step 11 and 2(i), ‖Dg(x) − Dg(a)‖ = ‖D(x) − D(a)‖ ≤ η ≤ ε/2.
- If x ∉ A: let b := π(x), so |x − b| = d(x) ≤ |x − a| and |b − a| ≤ 2|x − a| < δ. Since Σ_{c∈Z_x} w_c(x) = 1 and Σ_{c∈Z_x} Dw_c(x) = 0, step 9 gives
 Dg(x) − D(a) = Σ_{c∈Z_x} w_c(x)(D(b_c) − D(a)) + Σ_{c∈Z_x} (P_{b_c}(x) − P_b(x)) Dw_c(x).
 - First sum: for c ∈ Z_x, |b_c − a| ≤ 3|x − a| < δ, so ‖D(b_c) − D(a)‖ ≤ η by 2(i). Being a convex combination, the first sum has norm ≤ η.
 - Second sum: d(x) ≤ |x − a| < 1/4, so r(x) = d(x)/100. For c ∈ Z_x:
 * |b_c − b| ≤ |b_c − x| + |x − b| ≤ 3 d(x);
 * ‖D(b_c) − D(b)‖ ≤ ‖D(b_c) − D(a)‖ + ‖D(b) − D(a)‖ ≤ 2η;
 * |h(b_c) − h(b) − D(b)(b_c − b)| ≤ η|b_c − b| ≤ 3η d(x), by 2(ii), since b, b_c ∈ A lie within δ of a;
 * |x − b_c| ≤ 2 d(x).
 By step 1, |P_{b_c}(x) − P_b(x)| ≤ 3η d(x) + 2η·2 d(x) = 7η d(x) = 700 η r(x). With step 8, the second sum has norm ≤ 700 η r(x)·M/r(x) = 700 M η.
 Hence ‖Dg(x) − D(a)‖ ≤ η(1 + 700M) = ε/2 < ε.
So Dg is continuous at a.
13. (Conclusion.) By steps 9, 11 and 12, g is differentiable on ℝ^n with continuous derivative, so g ∈ C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 g, via contDiff_one_iff_fderiv). By step 9, g = h on A. By step 11, HasFDerivAt g (D a) a for every a ∈ A. ∎
proof_key_steps: If A = ∅, take g = 0. Otherwise use the radius r(x) = min(1, dist(x,A))/100, the affine jets P_b(x) = h(b) + D(b)(x − b) and nearest points π(x) ∈ A.
Compact-uniform compatibility on A ∩ B̄(a,1) plus continuity of D gives, near each a ∈ A, ‖D(b) − D(a)‖ ≤ η and |h(c) − h(b) − D(b)(c − b)| ≤ η|c − b| for anchors b, c within δ of a.
Vitali gives disjoint Whitney balls B(c, r(c)) whose 4-fold enlargements cover ℝ^n ∖ A. Radii of nearby centres are comparable, and the overlap is bounded by N = N(n).
Rescaled bumps φ_c, normalized to w_c = φ_c/Σφ, form a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^n ∖ A with Σ‖Dw_c(x)‖ ≤ M/r(x).
g = h on A and g = Σ w_c P_{π(c)} off A is smooth off A. Near a ∈ A, |g(x) − P_a(x)| ≤ ε|x − a| (so Dg(a) = D(a)) and ‖Dg(x) − D(a)‖ ≤ η(1 + 700M). Hence g ∈ C¹.
